result.topic: Automated / LLM-based review and validation of laboratory protocols and protocol code — positioning a deterministic validate->repair loop with a command-ledger conformance gate
result.metric_or_spec: Where existing protocol-review methods are WEAK — the gap our conformance ledger fills: (1) NO SOUND EXTERNAL GATE. Coscientist, ChemCrow, ORGANA, and Self-Refine adjudicate correctness with the same LLM that generated the plan; Stechly/Kambhampati (arXiv:2402.08115, ICLR 2025) and Huang et al. (arXiv:2310.01798, ICLR 2024) show this self-verification collapses on planning-shaped tasks — none inserts a deterministic, model-external verifier between generated commands and the instrument. (2) SCHEMA-VALID != PROCEDURALLY CORRECT. Autoprotocol/Aquarium/LabOP-SBOL validate representation (JSON schema, OWL/RDF consistency, PROV structure) but ship no checker that a protocol only uses allowed operations in a legal order with satisfied preconditions — a well-formed-but-wrong protocol passes. (3) SIMULATORS CHECK SYNTAX, NOT INTENT. OpentronsAI's simulator catches API/labware/tip errors but will happily simulate a valid-but-semantically-wrong procedure; there is no check that the emitted command sequence conforms to the intended protocol's ledger. (4) EVAL METRICS ARE SOFT AND NON-REPAIRING. BioPlanner and ProtoCode score per-step/per-field similarity or retrieval against ground truth (69-100% field accuracy) but neither hard-rejects nor repairs a nonconforming sequence; residual extraction error flows straight downstream. (5) MONITORING IS POST-DISPATCH. ORGANA detects failures via perception after commands are issued, not before. (6) TEST/VERIFIER QUALITY IS ITSELF UNVALIDATED. In the generated-code world, Ma et al. 'Rethinking Verification for LLM Code Generation: From Generation to Testing' (arXiv:2507.06920, TCGBench/SAGA, NeurIPS 2025) shows verification test suites are homogeneous and miss subtle faults — the analog of an incomplete command ledger. PROPOSED METRIC for our system: a Command-Ledger Conformance Rate — fraction of emitted instrument commands that (a) draw from the allowed-operation set, (b) satisfy declared preconditions/resource state, and (c) preserve the reference step-DAG ordering — computed by a deterministic, LLM-external checker, gating dispatch and driving a bounded validate->repair loop whose repair proposer is the LLM but whose accept/reject decision never is. Report ledger coverage (comprehensiveness of the allowed-operation set) alongside conformance to avoid the TCGBench 'homogeneous suite inflates pass rate' failure.

But its check is a soft similarity/retrieval metric over pseudofunctions, not a hard deterministic gate, and it evaluates plans rather than repairing them. Our contribution is turning that admissible-operation set into a deterministic validate->repair loop.

result.topic: Quantifying reproducibility/replication in laboratory science and automation — evidence base for a rigorous "replication percent" metric in Paper2Protocol
result.metric_or_spec:
PROPOSED COMPUTABLE "REPLICATION PERCENT" FOR PAPER2PROTOCOL.

Design principle (from OSC 2015 + Errington 2021): a replication score is meaningless without (i) a declared multi-criterion success rule and (ii) strict separation of 'could-not-attempt' (BLOCKED) from 'attempted-and-failed' and from 'silently-dropped'. So RP% is reported as a VECTOR, never a lone number: (RP%, BLOCKED%, SILENT-DROP%).

INPUTS (all from the analyze pass):
- A = set of IR assertions extracted from the paper's intermediate representation (each is a discrete, checkable claim: a step, a reagent/concentration target, a gate, or a handoff).
- L = commands[] ledger produced by analyze/lowering; each command carries postconditions and provenance back to zero+ assertions.
- Partition A into: R (realized — a ledger command satisfies the assertion's postcondition), B (honest-BLOCKED — flagged unrealizable: missing reagent, ambiguous/under-specified spec, unsupported op), D (silent-drop — in A but neither realized nor BLOCKED; the dishonest bucket, target = 0).
- Attemptable scope A* = A \ B.

FOUR TERMS (each a fraction in [0,1]):

1. Assertion realization  r_a = |R| / |A*|
   Fraction of attemptable IR assertions with a satisfied ledger command. This is the core NeurIPS/FAIR-style rubric fraction.

2. Concentration/unit fidelity  r_c = |{p in P* : dim_ok(p) AND |c_hat(p) - c_target(p)| / c_target(p) <= tau(class,p)}| / |P*|
   over preparation/quantitative assertions P* (attemptable subset). dim_ok is a HARD gate — dimensional/unit mismatch fails the step regardless of numeric closeness (catches the unit-error class). tau is the assay-class tolerance band, defaulted to the measured automated-liquid-handling CV (~1-5%, SLAS 2024; the measured envelope is CV 0.15-1.50% for larger volumes rising to 2-8% at ~1 uL, so tau should scale UP for sub-microliter transfers); this is the CI-style concordance rule borrowed from OSC 2015 ('realized value within tolerance band', not exact equality).

3. Gate/handoff completeness  r_g = |{i in I(class) : satisfied(i)}| / |I(class)|
   over the assay-class invariant set I(class) — the required controls/gates/handoffs for that assay type (e.g., qPCR requires a no-template-control gate; Western blot requires a loading-control normalization handoff; any transfer requires a volume/units-conserved handoff). Scored FAIR-maturity style as satisfied-fraction of required invariants.

4. Honesty factor  h = 1 - |D| / |A|
   Multiplicative penalty that rewards explicit BLOCKED over silent loss (Errington's separation). If nothing is silently dropped, h = 1.

COMPOSITE:
   RP% = 100 * h * ( w_a*r_a + w_c*r_c + w_g*r_g ),   w_a + w_c + w_g = 1
   Default weights w_a=0.40, w_c=0.30, w_g=0.30 (assertion realization weighted highest per Baker 2016: incomplete method specification is the dominant, fixable failure mode). Weights are assay-class configurable.

HARD VETO: any dim_ok failure or any unsatisfied SAFETY-critical invariant in I(class) caps RP% at a declared ceiling (e.g., 0 for the affected leg), so a numerically-close-but-dimensionally-wrong or unsafe protocol can never score high.

MANDATORY CO-REPORT (honesty accounting, non-negotiable):
   BLOCKED% = 100*|B|/|A|,  SILENT-DROP% = 100*|D|/|A|.
RP% is NEVER shown without BLOCKED%. A protocol that honestly BLOCKS 60% of assertions and perfectly realizes the rest reports e.g. RP%=100 over attemptable scope, BLOCKED%=60, SILENT-DROP%=0 — transparent, not inflated. This is the Errington rule made computable: attemptable-scope success and coverage are orthogonal axes and are always shown together.

WORKED SHAPE: |A|=100, B=15, D=0, A*=85. R=76 -> r_a=0.894. P*=30 quantitative, 27 within tau & dim_ok -> r_c=0.900. I(class)=12 invariants, 11 satisfied -> r_g=0.917. h=1. RP% = 100*1*(0.40*0.894 + 0.30*0.900 + 0.30*0.917) = 100*(0.3576+0.270+0.2751) = 90.3%. Report: (RP% 90.3, BLOCKED% 15, SILENT-DROP% 0).

verified_entries.citation: Baker M. 1,500 scientists lift the lid on reproducibility. Nature, 533(7604):452-454, 2016.
verified_entries.verify_note: Confirmed real. Nature vol 533, pp 452-454 (2016), DOI 10.1038/533452a, author Monya Baker. Verified via nature.com/articles/533452a, ADS 2016Natur.533..452B, and IDEAS/RePEc. Year, venue, DOI all correct.
verified_entries.key_findings: Survey of 1,576 researchers: ~90% agreed there is a reproducibility crisis (52% 'significant', 38% 'slight'); >70% had failed to reproduce another scientist's experiment and >50% had failed to reproduce one of their own. Ranked selective reporting, pressure to publish, low statistical power, insufficient replication, and poor method/protocol description as top contributors. Establishes that irreproducibility is dominated by under-specified methods and unreported parameters — exactly the assertions an IR ledger can make explicit.
verified_entries.relevance: Anchors WHY a replication-percent metric is needed and points the metric at the failure modes it can actually observe: unrecorded/under-specified method steps. Supports weighting assertion-realization and gate/handoff completeness heavily, since 'poor method description' is the #1 fixable cause.

verified_entries.citation: Open Science Collaboration (Nosek B.A. et al.). Estimating the reproducibility of psychological science. Science, 349(6251):aac4716, 2015.
verified_entries.verify_note: Confirmed real. Science vol 349, article aac4716 (2015), DOI 10.1126/science.aac4716. Verified via science.org and Tilburg research portal. Headline stats corroborated: 36% replicated by significance, 47% of original effect sizes within replication 95% CI, 39% subjectively judged to replicate, replication effects ~half of original. Entry's figures match.
verified_entries.key_findings: Replicated 100 studies. Reproducibility depended entirely on the metric chosen: 36% replicated by statistical-significance (same-direction p<0.05), 47% of original effect sizes fell inside the replication's 95% CI, and mean replication effect size was ~half the original (r=0.197 vs 0.403). Demonstrates that a single 'success rate' is meaningless without a stated definition, and that direction + confidence-interval/effect-size concordance are the defensible operationalizations.
verified_entries.relevance: Directly informs the replication-percent DEFINITION: use a declared, multi-criterion rule (direction match AND realized value within a tolerance band = CI-style concordance) rather than a bare pass/fail. Justifies reporting the metric as a vector with an explicit criterion, not one hero number.

verified_entries.citation: Errington T.M., Mathur M., Soderberg C.K., Denis A., Perfito N., Iorns E., Nosek B.A. Investigating the replicability of preclinical cancer biology. eLife, 10:e71601, 2021.
verified_entries.verify_note: Confirmed real. eLife 2021;10:e71601, DOI 10.7554/eLife.71601, verified via elifesciences.org/articles/71601 and ResearchGate. Companion paper 10.7554/eLife.67995 ('Challenges for assessing replicability in preclinical cancer biology', PubMed 34874008) also confirmed real. Scope figures (193 experiments from 53 papers selected; 50 experiments from 23 papers / 158 effects completed) verified. Year, venue, both DOIs correct.
verified_entries.key_findings: 50 experiments / 158 effects from 23 high-impact cancer papers. Under 5 dichotomous criteria, 46% of replications succeeded on more criteria than they failed; median replication effect size was 85% smaller than original; 92% of replication effects were smaller. Companion paper (10.7554/eLife.67995) reports that the project INTENDED 193 experiments from 53 papers but could only complete 50 — protocol incompleteness and reagent unavailability were the dominant reasons experiments could not be attempted.
verified_entries.relevance: The single most important source for HONEST-BLOCKED accounting. It separates 'could not be attempted' (protocol incomplete / reagent unavailable) from 'attempted and failed to replicate'. Paper2Protocol's metric must likewise never count a BLOCKED assertion as either success or silent failure — mirror Errington's separation of attemptable scope from realized scope.

verified_entries.verify_note: Confirmed real. Science vol 324, pp 85-89 (published 3 April 2009), DOI 10.1126/science.1165620, PubMed 19342587. verified_entries.relevance: Proof-of-concept that a machine-readable, assertion-level ledger of an experiment enables verifiable replication. Validates Paper2Protocol's approach of extracting IR assertions and checking realization against a commands[] ledger: the ledger is the provenance object that makes 'replication percent' computable rather than subjective.

Supports treating unit-correct realized concentrations and completed handoffs as the measurable substrate of replication.

verified_entries.relevance: This is the concrete 'Isaac Sim/Lab' option for the head-to-head. It is the only one of the candidate open frameworks that inherits PhysX GPU particle fluids and photoreal (RTX) rendering, i.e. the only path that can render liquid in wells and be optically believable as an OT-2 twin without adopting the whole Omniverse enterprise stack.

verified_entries.citation: Todorov, E., Erez, T., Tassa, Y. MuJoCo: A physics engine for model-based control. 2012 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS), pp. 5026-5033, 2012. (MJX / MuJoCo XLA GPU backend added in MuJoCo 3.0, 2023.)
verified_entries.verify_note: Confirmed via dblp/Semantic Scholar/IEEE. Todorov, Erez, Tassa, IROS 2012, Vilamoura-Algarve, pp. 5026-5033, DOI 10.1109/IROS.2012.6386109 — all exact. MJX GPU backend (MuJoCo 3.0, 2023) is a real, DeepMind-maintained addition.
verified_entries.key_findings: Generalized-coordinate multibody dynamics with a soft, well-conditioned convex contact model and analytically smooth (differentiable) forward/inverse dynamics — the gold standard for contact-rich control research. MJX re-expresses the whole solver as XLA/JAX primitives, so it runs thousands of differentiable envs on Nvidia/AMD GPUs, Apple Silicon, and TPUs at up to millions of steps/s. Now DeepMind/Google-maintained, fully open (Apache-2.0).
verified_entries.relevance: Best-in-class for the OT-2's mechanical realism: gantry kinematics, tip press-fit pickup contact, plate seating, and collision-safety, plus a huge RL ecosystem (robosuite, dm_control, MuJoCo Playground). Weakness for our twin: no native volumetric liquid — aqueous handling must be an analytical/bookkeeping model layered on top, not physically simulated.

verified_entries.citation: Genesis Embodied AI Consortium. Genesis: A Generative and Universal Physics Engine for Robotics and Beyond. Open-source project, Dec 2024.
verified_entries.verify_note: Confirmed as a real open-source project at github.com/Genesis-Embodied-AI/Genesis (README + genesis-world.readthedocs.io). Released Dec 2024, unified multi-physics (rigid, MPM, SPH, FEM, PBD, Stable Fluid). Correctly cited as a project, NOT a peer-reviewed paper — none exists as of 2026. Headline claim: >43M FPS on single RTX 4090 (self-reported).
verified_entries.key_findings: Unified multi-physics engine advertising rigid, articulated, MPM, SPH-style fluid, cloth and PBD solvers under one Python API, with headline claims of ~10-80x faster-than-realtime and very high parallel throughput on GPU. Uniquely among the candidates it aims to natively co-simulate rigid robots AND liquids/soft materials, plus a generative scene/asset pipeline. Young; benchmarks are largely self-reported and not yet independently validated for metrology-grade twins.
verified_entries.relevance: The most interesting single-engine answer to 'contact-rich robot + liquid in one solver,' which is exactly the OT-2 pipetting problem. Treat as a high-upside watch-item / prototype target, not yet the load-bearing twin — validation maturity and community support lag Isaac Sim and MuJoCo.

verified_entries.citation: Xiang, F., Qin, Y., Mo, K., Xia, Y., Zhu, H., Liu, F., Liu, M., Jiang, H., Yuan, Y., Wang, H., Yi, L., Chang, A.X., Guibas, L.J., Su, H. SAPIEN: A SimulAted Part-based Interactive ENvironment. CVPR 2020.
verified_entries.verify_note: Confirmed at CVPR 2020 Open Access (openaccess.thecvf.com) and Semantic Scholar. Full author list matches (Xiang, Qin, Mo, ... Guibas, Su). UCSD/Stanford/SFU collaboration, PhysX-backed articulated-object simulator.
verified_entries.key_findings: Physics-rich simulator built around a large corpus of articulated objects (PartNet-Mobility) with part-level kinematics and photorealistic ray-traced rendering. Provides the asset ecosystem and rendering backbone that ManiSkill builds on; strong for vision + interaction with articulated lab equipment (drawers, lids, doors).
verified_entries.relevance: Its articulated-asset library and rendering are attractive for modeling OT-2 accessories (deck modules, tip-rack lids, HEPA enclosure doors) and for training vision. Rigid/articulated-only: no native fluid, so it covers the mechanical and perceptual twin but not the liquid physics.

verified_entries.citation: Tao, S., Xiang, F., et al. (Hao Su Lab). ManiSkill3: GPU Parallelized Robotics Simulation and Rendering for Generalizable Embodied AI. 2024. Accepted ICLR 2025. (Prior: Gu et al., ManiSkill2, ICLR 2023.)
verified_entries.verify_note: Confirmed at https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.00425 — title and Hao Su Lab authorship match, submitted Oct 1 2024, accepted to ICLR 2025 (refinement: original entry called it only a preprint). Reports up to 30,000+ FPS and 10-1000x faster with 2-3x less GPU memory. ManiSkill2 (2302.04659, ICLR 2023) also real.
verified_entries.key_findings: SAPIEN-based, fully GPU-parallelized simulation AND rendering for contact-rich manipulation; reports up to 30,000+ FPS and 10-1000x faster state+visual throughput with 2-3x less GPU memory than competing platforms across 12 task domains. Ships thousands of assets, millions of demonstration frames, and standardized manipulation task families.
verified_entries.relevance: Strongest open option for fast, visual, contact-rich manipulation RL and for benchmarking the OT-2 gantry's pick/place and tip-handling policies at scale on modest GPUs. Like SAPIEN, rigid/articulated-focused — liquid handling would be abstracted, not physically simulated.

verified_entries.citation: Freeman, C.D., Frey, E., Raichuk, A., Girgin, S., Mordatch, I., Bachem, O. Brax — A Differentiable Physics Engine for Large Scale Rigid Body Simulation. NeurIPS 2021 Datasets & Benchmarks Track.
verified_entries.verify_note: Confirmed at https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.13281 — title and authors match (Freeman, Frey, Raichuk, Girgin, Mordatch, Bachem), NeurIPS D&B 2021, submitted Jun 24 2021. JAX-native, ships PPO/SAC/ES.
verified_entries.key_findings: JAX-native, differentiable rigid-body engine that co-compiles environment and learning algorithm (PPO/SAC/ES) onto the same accelerator for seamless massively-parallel RL on GPU/TPU. Prioritizes speed and end-to-end differentiability over contact fidelity.
verified_entries.relevance: Reference point for differentiable, JAX-based massively-parallel RL; useful if the twin's control loop is trained by gradient methods. For the OT-2 its softer contact model and rigid-only scope make it a research/prototyping engine rather than the fidelity twin — MJX is generally the stronger JAX choice today.

verified_entries.citation: Zhu, Y., Wong, J., Mandlekar, A., Martín-Martín, R., Joshi, A., Lin, K., Maddukuri, A., Nasiriany, S., Zhu, Y. robosuite: A Modular Simulation Framework and Benchmark for Robot Learning. 2020 (rev. 2022, 2025).
verified_entries.verify_note: Confirmed at https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.12293 and UT-Austin RPL page. Author list matches exactly (Yuke Zhu, Wong, Mandlekar, Martín-Martín, Joshi, Lin, Maddukuri, Nasiriany, Yifeng Zhu). MuJoCo-powered; actively maintained through v1.5.
verified_entries.key_findings: MuJoCo-powered modular framework with reusable robot/gripper/controller/task abstractions, operational-space and joint controllers, and reproducible manipulation benchmarks. The de-facto standard scaffolding for building custom MuJoCo manipulation environments.
verified_entries.relevance: Provides a ready-made modular pattern (robot + end-effector + controller + arena + task) to stand up an OT-2 environment on the MuJoCo/MJX backend quickly, with tested controllers you would otherwise reimplement.

verified_entries.citation: Tobin, J., Fong, R., Ray, A., Schneider, J., Zaremba, W., Abbeel, P. Domain Randomization for Transferring Deep Neural Networks from Simulation to the Real World. IROS 2017.
verified_entries.verify_note: Confirmed via dblp (TobinFRSZA17) and ACM DL (doi:10.1109/IROS.2017.8202133). Authors Tobin, Fong, Ray, Schneider, Zaremba, Abbeel; IROS 2017. arXiv:1703.06907 corresponds. ~1.5 cm detector accuracy claim verified in abstract.
verified_entries.key_findings: Founding domain-randomization paper: randomizing textures, lighting, camera and object poses in a non-photoreal simulator let a detector trained only on synthetic RGB localize real objects to ~1.5 cm with no real training images. Core idea: enough simulated variability makes reality look like just another sample.
verified_entries.relevance: The methodological backbone for making any OT-2 twin transfer: randomize deck lighting, plate/labware appearance, camera pose, tip/liquid optical properties and physical parameters (friction, tip-fit force, liquid viscosity/surface tension) so a policy or perception model trained in sim survives the real deck.

verified_entries.citation: OpenAI: Andrychowicz, M., Baker, B., Chociej, M., Józefowicz, R., McGrew, B., Pachocki, J., Petron, A., Plappert, M., Powell, G., Ray, A., Schneider, J., Sidor, S., Tobin, J., Welinder, P., Weng, L., Zaremba, W. Learning Dexterous In-Hand Manipulation. Int. J. Robotics Research 39(1), 2020 (preprint 2018). Follow-up: Solving Rubik's Cube with a Robot Hand (ADR), 2019.
verified_entries.verify_note: Confirmed at https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.00177 and IJRR (journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/0278364919887447, 2020). Full 16-author OpenAI list matches. Shadow Hand, MuJoCo, domain randomization for zero-shot sim-to-real. ADR follow-up (1910.07113) real.
verified_entries.key_findings: Landmark zero-shot sim-to-real: a Shadow Hand policy trained entirely in MuJoCo transferred to hardware purely via extensive domain randomization plus careful sim calibration; the 2019 sequel adds Automatic Domain Randomization (ADR), which grows randomization ranges automatically as the policy improves. Emphasizes that action delays, actuator/latency modeling and randomization schedules — not photorealism — drive successful transfer.
verified_entries.relevance: Directly informs the sim-to-real recipe for an OT-2 twin: model actuator dynamics and command latency of the gantry/pipette, and use ADR-style automatic randomization of physical parameters. Also a cautionary datapoint on the compute cost of brute-force randomization.

verified_entries.citation: Zhao, W., Queralta, J.P., Westerlund, T. Sim-to-Real Transfer in Deep Reinforcement Learning for Robotics: a Survey. 2020 IEEE Symposium Series on Computational Intelligence (SSCI), pp. 737-744.
verified_entries.verify_note: Confirmed at https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.13303. Authors Zhao, Peña Queralta, Westerlund; IEEE SSCI 2020, pp. 737-744. arXiv v1 Sep 2020, v2 Jul 2021.
verified_entries.key_findings: Structured survey of the reality gap and the main closing strategies — domain randomization, domain adaptation, imitation learning, meta-learning, knowledge distillation — plus practical transfer tips (model action delays, avoid bang-bang control, system identification).
verified_entries.relevance: One-stop map of transfer techniques and their tradeoffs to structure the OT-2 twin's validation plan, and to justify choosing system-identification/domain-adaptation over pure randomization where calibration data from the real deck is available.

verified_entries.citation: Macklin, M., Müller, M. Position Based Fluids. ACM Transactions on Graphics (SIGGRAPH) 32(4), Article 104, 2013.
verified_entries.verify_note: Confirmed at ACM DL (dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/2461912.2461984) and SIGGRAPH history archives. Macklin & Müller, ACM TOG vol. 32, issue 4, article 104, July 2013. DOI exact.
verified_entries.key_findings: Recasts SPH incompressibility as position-based-dynamics density constraints, giving stable large-timestep, real-time fluid with an artificial-pressure term for clumping-free particle distribution and surface tension. The algorithmic core of GPU particle fluids in FleX / PhysX / Isaac Sim.
verified_entries.relevance: This is the actual method that would simulate aqueous liquid particles in wells and tips inside an Isaac Sim OT-2 twin. Surface tension and incompressibility handling matter for realistic aspirate/dispense menisci and droplet behavior — but PBF is visually-plausible, not metrologically exact, so it validates behavior/geometry, not sub-microliter dosing accuracy.

verified_entries.citation: Macklin, M., Müller, M., Chentanez, N., Kim, T.-Y. Unified Particle Physics for Real-Time Applications. ACM Transactions on Graphics (SIGGRAPH) 33(4), 2014. (Basis of NVIDIA FleX; NVIDIA FleX 1.1 documentation.)
verified_entries.verify_note: Confirmed at ACM DL (dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/2601097.2601152) and SIGGRAPH history archives. Macklin, Müller, Chentanez, Kim, ACM TOG vol. 33 issue 4, 2014. DOI exact. Won the 2025 ACM SIGGRAPH Test-of-Time award.
verified_entries.key_findings: Single particle representation unifying rigid bodies, granular media, cloth, and position-based fluids with two-way coupling, shipped as NVIDIA FleX and later folded into PhysX/Omniverse particle systems. Enables one solver to handle a container, a tip, and the liquid together with mutual interaction. Recipient of the 2025 SIGGRAPH Test-of-Time award.
verified_entries.relevance: Explains why Isaac Sim can co-simulate the labware (rigid) and the aqueous liquid (fluid particles) with two-way coupling in one scene — the technical reason Isaac Sim is the fidelity choice for the liquid leg. FleX itself is legacy/standalone; in a modern twin you consume this capability through Isaac Sim/PhysX particles.
